analysis:
The change is documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md, with a date bump at line 3 and new text at head lines 684-691 (patch hunk @@ -681,6 +681,14), plus later hunks that are only partly visible. I examined the two supplied head-text units, lines 1-801. No code, config or enforcement paths changed.

The notable addition is the GLM5Next verified weight hash. After every manifest file matches, the load publishes the manifest aggregate (`GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256`) instead of separate WeightHasher passes. `VerifiedWeightHashStore` lets the next coordinator-mode start register that hash without reading the weights while each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged. The text says the load verifies again before serving. This touches T-012 (operator replaces weights), T-027 (weight substitution) and T-034 (self-reported identity). A stat-tuple cache could be bypassed by an operator who preserves metadata, for example by an in-place edit with timestamps restored. The ctime check mitigates this, but ctime can change through clock manipulation by a privileged operator. The documented re-verification before serving is the compensating control. Whether that re-verification really hashes file contents, and whether the registered hash reaches the coordinator before it is re-checked, cannot be confirmed from the docs alone. The implementation is not in the supplied evidence, so I record this as an unverified contract and not a finding.

The rest of the supplied text (Nemotron Super slot, prefix bank, cache scope partitioning, media admission limits) describes pre-existing behavior. It states that coordinator prefix reuse is partitioned by authenticated cache scope and off without one (T-041, consistent with the threat model), and that the slot emits no cache receipts.

A follow-up should check the code behind `VerifiedWeightHashStore` and `ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash` for cache invalidation, storage permissions and tamper resistance. The video-timing documentation changes at head lines 818-821 and the later hunks were not fully visible.
